about.tagline: The most complete bot for Twitch and Kick streamers
about.intro: Decatron is an all-in-one platform that lets you manage commands, overlays, alerts, giveaways and much more. Designed by streamers, for streamers.
about.audienceIntro: Decatron is designed for Twitch and Kick streamers who want:

audience.d: An intuitive interface and ready-to-use commands from day one
A powerful scripting system to build complex commands

features.d: Dynamic variables, advanced scripting and micro commands to automate your chat
Timers with overlay, alerts, progress bars and automatic events
A complete raffle system with requirements, weights and history
Custom notifications for follows, subs, raids, bits and more
Show channel information with a clip preview and statistics
Word filters, a strike system and automatic actions
Ask the AI with !ia in the chat, and talk with it from your dashboard

about.ctaText: Connect your Twitch or Kick account and start using Decatron in minutes. The bot, the commands and the overlays are free, with no credit card.

features.title: All of Decatron's features
features.subtitle: Explore all the tools available to boost your stream.
features.ctaText: Connect your Twitch or Kick account and start using all these features in minutes.

default.d: Ready-to-use commands: !game, !title, !so, !followage and many more. Configurable, with custom permissions.

custom.d: Create your own commands with dynamic variables. Use $(user), $(game), $(uptime) and more for smart replies.

micro.d: Chat shortcuts to change the stream category. You type !apex and the stream switches to Apex Legends.

scripting.d: Create commands with conditional logic, loops and variables. The most powerful scripting system for Twitch bots.

timer.d: Professional timers with overlay, progress bars, completion alerts and automatic events.

eventAlerts.d: Visual and audio notifications for follows, subs, bits, raids and more. Level and variant system.

giveaway.d: Raffles with participation requirements, weights that raise the chance of winning and history.

sound.d: Assign a sound, video or image to each channel points reward (Twitch and Kick).

tips.d: Receive donations with PayPal. Customizable page, alerts and timer integration.

shoutout.d: Show information about other channels with a preview of their latest clip and statistics.

moderation.d: Banned words, links, spam, panic mode and strikes on Twitch and Kick, with commands for your mods and a history with undo.

ai.d: The !ia command answers questions in your chat, and Decatron Chat lets you talk with the AI from the dashboard.

analytics.d: Timer events, moderation actions, game and title changes, chat messages, followers and tips, with CSV export.

followers.d: Follower list synced with Twitch, with unfollows, returned followers, search and filters.

start.title: Getting started with Decatron
start.subtitle: In just 5 minutes you will have your bot set up and running on your Twitch or Kick channel.
req: A Twitch or Kick account (streamer or creator)
A modern web browser (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari)

s1.t: Sign in with Twitch or Kick
s1.d: Click the sign-in button and authorize Decatron to access your account.
s1.note: Decatron only requests the permissions it needs to work. You can revoke access at any time from your Twitch or Kick account.

s2.d: Once connected, you will be redirected to the dashboard where you can customize your bot.

items.d: Turn commands like !game, !title, !so on or off
Turn the bot on or off in your channel from Settings → Channel and bot
Choose the language of the interface and of the bot's messages
Set who can use each command

s3.d: Go to your Twitch chat and type the command to check that the bot is working (changing the title is not available on Kick yet).
s3.ok: Current title: My first stream with Decatron
s3.alert: If you see the answer in the chat, congratulations! Your bot is set up correctly.

s4.d: Overlays are visual elements you can add to your stream in OBS.
s4.intro: To add the timer overlay to OBS:
steps: Open OBS Studio and go to the scene where you want the overlay
Click "+" in Sources and select "Browser"
Copy the overlay URL from your dashboard
Paste the URL in OBS and adjust the size (the one the panel shows; 1920x1080 for most)
s4.tip: Turn on "Refresh browser when scene becomes active" so the overlay refreshes automatically.

start.next: You have the basics set up. Now explore all the features Decatron has to offer.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Answers to the most common questions about Decatron
faq.ctaTitle: Did not find what you were looking for?
faq.ctaText: Check the full documentation or contact us directly.

items.a: Decatron is an all-in-one bot for Twitch and Kick that lets you manage commands, overlays, alerts, giveaways and much more. It is designed to be easy to use, with advanced options for experienced streamers.

The bot, the commands and the overlays are free. Features that have a real cost for the platform (AI, premium voice, live translation, LoL coach) are paid with credits, and the support plans only expand quantities (more accounts, more variants, faster refresh); they never lock features.
Decatron works in all modern browsers: Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari and Opera. We recommend using the latest version of your browser for the best experience.

items.q: How do I connect the bot to my channel?
items.intro: Connecting Decatron to your channel is very simple:
steps: Click "Sign in" on the main page
Authorize Decatron with your Twitch or Kick account
The bot will connect to your channel automatically

items.q: Can I use the bot on multiple channels?
items.a: One Decatron account can join your Twitch channel and your Kick channel and switch between them from Settings. If someone gives you access to their channel, you can also configure it from your account with the level they assign you.

items.q: The bot does not answer commands, what do I do?
items.intro: If the bot does not answer, check the following:
steps: Make sure you have signed in and the bot is connected (green indicator in the dashboard)
Check that the command exists and is enabled
Check that you have the permissions needed to use that command
Check that there is no active cooldown
items.tip: Try the !title command in the chat (if you are a moderator or the streamer). If it does not answer, there is a connection problem.

items.q: How do I create a custom command?
steps: Go to Commands → Custom in the dashboard
Click "New command"
Type the command name (without the !)
Type the reply, using variables if you like
Set permissions and cooldown
Save the command

items.q: Which variables can I use in commands?
items.a: Decatron has many variables available such as $(user), $(game), $(uptime), $(followage) and more. Each variable is replaced automatically with its value in real time.

items.q: How do I add overlays to OBS?
items.intro: To add an overlay to OBS:
steps: Open OBS Studio
In the scene where you want the overlay, click "+" in Sources
Select "Browser"
Give it a name and click OK
Copy the overlay URL from your dashboard
Paste the URL in the "URL" field
Adjust the width and height (the one that overlay's panel shows; 1920x1080 for most)
Click OK
items.note: Overlays have a transparent background, so you can place them over your scene.

items.q: The overlays do not update, what do I do?
items.intro: If the overlays do not update:
steps: Right-click the browser source in OBS
Select "Refresh"
If the problem persists, select "Properties" and turn on "Refresh browser when scene becomes active"

items.q: How do I report a bug?
items.a: You can report bugs by creating an issue in the GitHub repository. Include as many details as possible: what you were doing, what you expected to happen and what actually happened.

items.q: Where can I request new features?
items.a: Feature suggestions are welcome as issues on GitHub. We review all suggestions and prioritize the ones the community asks for most.

api.authIntro: Decatron uses OAuth 2.0 with the Authorization Code flow. It is the safest flow for applications that can keep a secret.
flow: Your app redirects the user to /oauth/authorize
The user sees the requested permissions and approves or denies
Decatron redirects the user back with a temporary code
Your server exchanges the code for tokens at /api/oauth/token
Use the access_token to call the API
api.pkceIntro: For public applications (mobile, SPA), use PKCE for extra security:
api.refreshIntro: Access tokens expire in 1 hour. Use the refresh token to get a new one:
api.revokeIntro: To invalidate a token (for example, when the user signs out):
api.scopesIntro: Scopes define what your application can do. Request only the ones you need.

rows: Live category, title, viewers and latest follower
Start, pause and stop the timer
Send chat messages (requires the app to be verified)
Create a marker on the stream

Exchanges the code for tokens or refreshes tokens

errors: The token does not have the required scopes
Too many requests (only on public routes that have a limit)
api.limits: The public v1 API has no global request limit. Only some public routes (for example, tournament registration or card images) have their own limits and answer 429 when exceeded.
